description: How one stored transcript line reads: as Swift's JSONDecoder decoded a TranscriptEntry with .secondsSince1970 dates. The line must scan as a JSON document (UTF-8 after one optional byte order mark, or UTF-16/UTF-32; space, tab, LF and CR around tokens; one trailing comma) whose root is an object with every key convertible. Then id must be a string that UUID(uuidString:) accepts (36 ASCII characters, hex digits of either case in 8-4-4-4-12 groups; returned uppercase), kind exactly one of user, assistant, tool, system, error, text a string and date a Double (a number that converts as config/round-trip.json pins: overflow, underflow and Foundation's true-zero quirk fail). Of equal keys the first wins; other members are ignored and never converted. Any failure skips the line.
function: TranscriptStore line decoding — input one line without its newline (a string, or {"hex": <bytes>}), expected the transcript entry {id, kind, text, date} it reads as (date the seconds since 1970 that JSONDecoder read), or null when the line is skipped
verifiedBy: DESIGN.md v1.6, v2.14; Tests/PowerUpTests/TranscriptFixtureTests.swift testTranscriptLineTable writes the line to a temporary transcript file and loads it through TranscriptStore.loadTail (the date compared as the Date built from the expected seconds). Rust: rust/powerup-core/tests/transcript.rs transcript_line_cases runs transcript::decode_line on the bytes and compares the entry (the date by value).
capturedAgainst: Swift 5.9.2 JSONDecoder, JSONEncoder and CryptoKit (Xcode 15.2) on macOS 27.2, PowerUp at 0bc961f

cases.name: a canonical line
cases.reason: The line the core writes reads back as the same entry.

cases.name: members in another order
cases.reason: Swift wrote the members in hash order, which changed from launch to launch; a line is read by key, so every old line loads (HK-416).

cases.name: every kind reads: assistant
cases.reason: assistant is one of the five kinds.

cases.name: every kind reads: tool
cases.reason: tool is one of the five kinds.

cases.name: every kind reads: system
cases.reason: system is one of the five kinds.

cases.name: every kind reads: error
cases.reason: error is one of the five kinds.

cases.name: a lowercase id reads, uppercased
cases.reason: UUID(uuidString:) takes either case; the entry holds the UUID, which is written back in uppercase.

cases.name: a mixed-case id reads
cases.reason: Hex digits of either case mix freely.

cases.name: an id in braces is skipped
cases.reason: UUID(uuidString:) takes no braces, so the line does not decode.

cases.name: a compact id is skipped
cases.reason: The 32-digit form without hyphens is not a uuidString.

cases.name: a 37-character id is skipped
cases.reason: Exactly 36 characters, 8-4-4-4-12.

cases.name: an id with a space is skipped
cases.reason: No surrounding whitespace is trimmed from the id.

cases.name: an id with a non-hex digit is skipped
cases.reason: Only 0-9, a-f and A-F are hex digits.

cases.name: an id with full-width digits is skipped
cases.reason: A full-width digit is not an ASCII hex digit.

cases.name: an id with hyphens moved is skipped
cases.reason: The hyphens must stand at 8, 13, 18 and 23.

cases.name: an empty id is skipped
cases.reason: An empty string is not a UUID.

cases.name: a numeric id is skipped
cases.reason: The id must be a string.

cases.name: a missing id is skipped
cases.reason: Every member is required.

cases.name: a capitalized kind is skipped
cases.reason: The kind must be spelled exactly; Kind(rawValue:) is case-sensitive.

cases.name: an unknown kind is skipped
cases.reason: A kind from a future build is skipped, never guessed (HK-175).

cases.name: a numeric kind is skipped
cases.reason: The kind must be a string.

cases.name: a missing text is skipped
cases.reason: Every member is required.

cases.name: a null text is skipped
cases.reason: text is not optional, so null fails the line.

cases.name: a numeric text is skipped
cases.reason: The text must be a string.

cases.name: an empty text reads
cases.reason: An empty text is still a string.

cases.name: an integer date reads
cases.reason: An integer literal is a Double.

cases.name: a zero date reads
cases.reason: Zero is a valid date (1970).

cases.name: a negative date reads
cases.reason: A date before 1970 is still a Double.

cases.name: an exponent date reads
cases.reason: An exponent is valid number grammar.

cases.name: a string date is skipped
cases.reason: The date must be a number; .secondsSince1970 reads a Double.

cases.name: a bool date is skipped
cases.reason: A bool is not a Double for JSONDecoder.

cases.name: a null date is skipped
cases.reason: The date is not optional.

cases.name: a missing date is skipped
cases.reason: Every member is required.

cases.name: an overflowing date is skipped
cases.reason: A number past Double's range fails its field, so the line.

cases.name: an underflowing date is skipped
cases.reason: A nonzero literal that rounds to zero fails the Double conversion.

cases.name: a subnormal date reads
cases.reason: A subnormal Double is kept.

cases.name: 0e5 as a date is skipped
cases.reason: Foundation's true-zero check misreads 0e5 as an underflow (HK-413).

cases.name: 0.0e5 as a date reads
cases.reason: The same check accepts 0.0e5 as zero.

cases.name: a malformed date is skipped
cases.reason: A leading zero passes the scan but fails the Double conversion.

cases.name: extra members are ignored
cases.reason: Members the entry does not read are ignored, even one whose number is malformed, since JSONDecoder converts only what it reads.

cases.name: an extra member with a bad escape is ignored
cases.reason: An unread string is never unescaped.

cases.name: of two texts the first wins
cases.reason: JSONDecoder keeps the first of equal keys.

cases.name: a trailing comma reads
cases.reason: JSONDecoder accepts one trailing comma in an object.

cases.name: a byte order mark reads
cases.reason: JSONDecoder skips a UTF-8 byte order mark at the start of the line.

cases.name: a CR before the line's end reads
cases.reason: A file written with CRLF splits on LF; the CR is whitespace after the object.

cases.name: spaces around and inside read
cases.reason: Space, tab, LF and CR may stand between tokens.

cases.name: an escaped slash reads
cases.reason: \/ is a slash; the encoder writes every slash that way.

cases.name: an escaped newline reads
cases.reason: A newline in the text is escaped, so one entry is one line.

cases.name: escaped quotes and backslashes read
cases.reason: Escapes unescape.

cases.name: a unicode escape reads
cases.reason: A \u escape and a surrogate pair unescape to their scalars.

cases.name: raw non-ASCII reads
cases.reason: Non-ASCII, U+2028 included, is written raw and read raw.

cases.name: a leading byte order mark inside the text is kept
cases.reason: JSONDecoder keeps a U+FEFF at the start of a string.

cases.name: an escaped NUL reads
cases.reason: \u0000 is a valid escape.

cases.name: an invalid escape in the text is skipped
cases.reason: A bad escape fails the text, so the line.

cases.name: a raw tab in the text is skipped
cases.reason: A raw control character inside a string fails it.

cases.name: a lone surrogate escape is skipped
cases.reason: An unpaired surrogate fails the string.

cases.name: invalid UTF-8 in the text is skipped
cases.reason: Invalid UTF-8 fails the string.

cases.name: a bad escape in a key is skipped
cases.reason: The root's keys are all converted when the entry reads its keyed container, so one bad key fails the line.

cases.name: UTF-16LE text reads
cases.reason: JSONDecoder detects UTF-16 from the zero bytes, line by line.

cases.name: not JSON is skipped
cases.reason: A corrupt line is skipped (HK-175).

cases.name: an unrelated object is skipped
cases.reason: A line of another shape is skipped (HK-175).

cases.name: an array is skipped
cases.reason: The root must be an object.

cases.name: null is skipped
cases.reason: The root must be an object.

cases.name: an empty object is skipped
cases.reason: Every member is required.

cases.name: text after the object is skipped
cases.reason: Anything but whitespace after the root fails the line.

cases.name: two objects on one line are skipped
cases.reason: One line holds one entry.

cases.name: a truncated line is skipped
cases.reason: A line cut short by a crash mid-write is skipped.
